subject.title: Feature: configurable mediaLocalRoots for image tool

question: Which local filesystem/media-root policy should OpenClaw expose for image and media tools: shared tools.fs roots, scoped channel inbound roots only, or a narrow media-only allowlist?
rationale: The choice defines a public config surface and host filesystem read boundary, and the current code already shows separate partial designs with different security and compatibility tradeoffs.

options.title: Adopt shared tools.fs roots
options.body: Use or repair the open tools.fs.roots design as the canonical policy for file tools and media surfaces, with explicit security docs and upgrade tests.

options.title: Keep only scoped inbound roots
options.body: Treat iMessage attachment access as solved by channel-scoped roots and decline broad host-local media root configuration for now.

options.title: Add media-only allowlist
options.body: Approve a narrower tools.media or tools.image localRoots config, accepting the cost of a separate media trust boundary.

recommendation.title: Adopt shared tools.fs roots
recommendation.body: Use or repair the open tools.fs.roots design as the canonical policy for file tools and media surfaces, with explicit security docs and upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history on the filesystem policy and outbound media access boundary that this decision extends.
